questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Famous artists who only became famous after they died
Henrietta Lacks, whose cells made many discoveries possible
The history of the polio vaccine and how it reached Africa
How cancer is diagnosed and treated in hospitals today
questions.why: They tell the story of Henrietta Lacks, whose cells led to many medical breakthroughs.

questions.q: What do Van Gogh, Galileo and Henrietta Lacks have in common?
options: They were all scientists who worked together
They all lived and worked in America
They all died of cancer at a young age
They were recognised only after death
questions.why: Rob says their contributions were only recognised after their death, and Georgina adds Henrietta.

questions.q: What was extraordinary about Henrietta Lacks' cells?
options: They could not be infected by viruses
They were very large
They could keep replacing themselves endlessly
They glowed in the dark
questions.why: Doctors found her cells could replace themselves endlessly.

questions.q: Did Henrietta Lacks agree to her cells being used for research?
options: No, she never gave her consent
Yes, she asked doctors to use them
Yes, her family agreed for her
Yes, but only for cancer research
questions.why: Rob says she never consented to her tissues being used for medical research.

questions.q: According to Rebecca Skloot, how have HeLa cells helped with Covid?
options: They were used to make face masks for hospitals
They helped show what the virus's receptor is like
They cured the first Covid patients
They showed that Covid came from bats
questions.why: She says scientists quickly figured out what the receptor looks like using her cells.

questions.q: Why does Rebecca Skloot call HeLa cells a 'workhorse'?
options: Because the cells were first tested on horses in a lab
Because they are very strong and hard to destroy
Because they are cheap and easy for labs to buy
Because they are at the base of so much science
questions.why: She calls them 'this incredible workhorse that is at the base of so much science'.

questions.q: What recent news does Sir John Burn think Henrietta would have liked?
options: The polio vaccine had wiped out polio in Africa
A new cancer drug was discovered
Her family received money
A book about her became a best-seller
questions.why: He says she would have liked the announcement that the polio vaccine led to polio's eradication in Africa.

questions.q: Why does Sir John Burn describe her contribution as 'unwitting'?
options: Because it was a mistake
Because nobody used her cells
Because it was made without her knowledge
Because she was not a scientist
questions.why: Georgina explains it was made without her knowledge or consent.
